title: Latest telematics improves regional council operations
summary:
MacDonnell Regional Council delivers essential services to some of Australia’s most remote and challenging environments. The council supports 13 remote communities in the Northern Territory — across a region comparable in size to Victoria — and delivers services including road maintenance, waste management, water services, community safety, aged care and early learning.

Operating a fleet of approximately 340 vehicles and assets, alongside a workforce of around 500 employees, creates a complex operating environment in which employees can travel distances of up to 700 km a day from head office to reach remote communities, often across rough, unsealed roads without cellular coverage and in highly unpredictable conditions.

To support these operations, the council needed a better way to:

  • protect the safety of employees working in isolated and hazardous conditions
  • maintain visibility of vehicles travelling through areas without mobile coverage
  • improve fleet utilisation and reduce unnecessary vehicle purchases
  • prevent the theft and misuse of vehicles and equipment in remote communities
  • monitor how vehicles were being driven on harsh roads
  • streamline maintenance and better understand vehicle lifecycle data.
     

Previous providers were unable to deliver reliable hardware performance or provide the level of support required, resulting in issues including device failures, battery drain and limited usability. The council needed a new solution that could operate effectively in extreme conditions while being simple to deploy and use at scale.

MacDonnell Regional Council implemented a comprehensive fleet and asset management solution tailored to its requirements and based at its core on Teletrac Navman’s GPS tracking and telematics platform. Enhanced with satellite connectivity, the platform is designed to ensure continuous visibility and communication even in areas without cellular coverage.

The solution enables the council to maintain real-time visibility of vehicles and assets across its operating region, including in areas without cellular coverage, monitor driver behaviour in challenging conditions, and improve how fleet resources are allocated and managed. It also supports stronger oversight of plant and equipment in remote communities, helping reduce misuse and unauthorised access.

The system also allows teams to set expected travel timeframes and monitor whether staff reach destinations safely, providing an additional layer of oversight for long-distance, high-risk travel.

Implementation was supported by hands-on training and ongoing consultation, ensuring strong adoption across departments. The onboarding process was described as simple and highly manageable, with the intuitive interface and mobile app making it easy for teams to create profiles, access data, and use the system effectively.

Unlike typical fleet deployments, MacDonnell Regional Council leverages nearly all capabilities of the Teletrac Navman software platform, using it not only for tracking, but also for safety, governance, maintenance, utilisation and operational decision making.

“Safety is the biggest priority for us. Our fleet can be replaced, but people can’t. With Teletrac Navman, we know where our teams are, how they’re travelling, and that they can call for help if anything goes wrong,” said Jake Potter, MacDonnell Regional Council. “The system gives us exactly what we asked for, from tracking and safety through to understanding how our vehicles are used and managed.

“The onboarding was straightforward, and the platform is simple to roll out and straightforward for our teams to use. Most importantly, the level of visibility we now have across such a large and remote area is critical to how we operate.”

MacDonnell Regional Council says it has realised significant operational and safety benefits from the system upgrade, including enhanced worker safety in remote environments, full visibility beyond cellular networks, improved fleet utilisation and cost control, reduced theft and asset misuse, better driving behaviour and asset care, streamlined maintenance and lifecycle management, and improved service delivery efficiency.

title: Quest Software completes IRAP assessments
summary:
Data management and cybersecurity company Quest Software has achieved Infosec Registered Assessors Program (IRAP) authorisations for handling government data up to the protected classification level.

The independent assessment was completed for both the Quest Trusted Data Management Platform and the Quest Security Management Platform. The certification means both platforms have been evaluated against the Australian Signals Directorate’s Information Security Manual, and will make it easier for government departments to procure the solutions.

Quest Software Head of APAC Richard Kulkarni said many of Australia’s largest government agencies already run the company’s technology in their on-premises environments.

“This IRAP assessed status doesn’t introduce Quest to government, rather it extends a relationship that already exists into hybrid and cloud-first territory, with independent assurance attached,” he said. “This is important because the modernisation that agencies are embarking on rarely looks like a single clean lift-and-shift.

“It looks like Active Directory and Entra ID modernisation running alongside Machinery of Government changes, cybersecurity uplift programs, and legacy platform retirement — often at the same time — with strict governance requirements and close to zero tolerance for downtime.” 

The Quest Security Management Platform is designed to support the monitoring, recovery and privileged access oversight of identities, while the Quest Data Management Platform aims to help agencies catalogue and turn their data into reusable, AI-ready data products.

title: Why AI Resilience Is Becoming a Critical Priority for Government Cybersecurity
summary:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming part of how state and local governments operate. Agencies are using AI to improve employee productivity, analyze data, strengthen cybersecurity operations and support citizen services.
